#3803. Fish with a sniper rifle takes aim at Tim Sweeney's hopes and dreams, as genAI-free meme game tops Epic Games' vibe-coding megajam

Epic Games are, as you're probably aware, going big on genAI at the moment. To the extent that, last month, the Tim Sweeney-helmed company announced the Epic AI MegaJam. Build a playable game in Unreal Engine or Unreal Editor for Fortnite with help from as many AI agents or tools as you like was the pitch.

So, naturally, sorting the submissions by 'Popular' turns up a game about a fish with a sniper rifle whose creator says they deliberately made it without using any generative AI.

The game's called LSD:FIH and sees a cigarette-smoking bit of shoe-wearing marine life go full MLG and start pulling off trickshots on blobs. If you struggled to parse that, you'll probably struggle even more with developer PolyCube's description of it as being a "computer game about a fih aura-farming". "No AI was used to make this game," is the other line in their description, which is far easier to parse.

"I made a game for the Epic's 'vibe-coding gamejam' megajam without using any AI in four days," they expanded on not Bluesky. "Sorta ran out of time so gameplay didn't turn out how I wanted, but hey it's still pretty aura."

Other submissions the megajam included a game called THIS GAME IS AI SLOP and one dubbed Goon Patrol - Director's Cut. If you're wondering how a game without genAI use could be allowed to stand among the slop masterpieces, it's because Epic ended up having to make clearer not long after the jam was announced that submissions didn't have to make use of genAI as a hard rule, leaving it up to the developer how much or little was worked in.

Still, I imagine noted genAI advocate Tim Sweeney's not best pleased that a game deliberately swimming against the slop tide shows up at the top if you hit up the Popular filter. Then again, he's been very busy posting important things about the situation with Jensen Huang and Nvidia lately, so maybe he hasn't noticed.

Yes, the last post I've linked there is the Sweens giggling at an AI image of him, Huang, Johan Andersson, and John Carmack as the heads carved into Mount Rushmore that he himself asked Grok to generate. As you do.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Knights of the Old Republic is my favorite RPG of all time, and a key reason why my love of video games developed as deeply as it did. My hopes for Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, a spiritual successor to BioWare's classic, are sky-high, and expectations from the broader community are similarly intense. Director Casey Hudson isn't too worried about that pressure, though – after all, he and much of the team at Arcanaut Studios made the original KOTOR and the Mass Effect trilogy.

"I think it would be really weird to do if I hadn't worked on the first one," Hudson admits in an interview for The Fourth Curtain podcast. "It would feel really strange. But I think, for us, we've got folks on the team who worked on that game and have worked on all the Mass Effect games since and other BioWare stuff."

Hudson says that experience "helps," because the studio knows "why we did things the way we did. We're not trying to fill someone else's shoes, despite the expectations being really high."

We still know very little about Fate of the Old Republic, other than the fact that it's a spiritual successor to KOTOR. What kind of gameplay systems will it build on? I can't imagine KOTOR's creaky D&D 3.5-based mechanics are going to make a comeback. What kind of story will it tell? It's going to have to be something all-new, with the entire Star Wars universe having been rebooted since KOTOR was new.

"The thing that supersedes everything is our passion and excitement for doing something amazing," Hudson says. "That has to outshine everything else, because you can't really know how to answer pressure, and it's hard to even really understand what other people want to play. But if you're so excited about making something that people are going to love, you're just passionate about it being amazing, that leads you to where you want to go."

That's maybe an obvious answer, but I appreciate that it's the one Hudson is providing. No new game can possibly live up to my nostalgic memories of BioWare's Star Wars RPG, and what I really want is a new game created by a team of people who are excited about what they're making. If it can tap into my old love for KOTOR, that's just icing on the cake.

#3801. Ubisoft lay off 166 more staff, this time at their Montreal and Quebec City studios, while mumbling about "current production priorities and business needs"

"Our production needs are changing," publishers claim

Ubisoft have laid off 166 developers, with this latest round of cuts at the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publishers taking place at two of their studios in Eastern Canada. Both studios affected, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, had a hand in last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows, with Montreal especially being a major and long-tenured development hub for the company.

Both IGN and GamesIndustry.biz report that the cuts, which amount to just under 4% studios' total combined headcount, affected staff working on recently cancelled or significantly changed projects.

"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," Ubisoft said in a statement handed to both sites. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources."

Ubisoft Montreal are currently working on Assassin’s Creed Hexe, reportedly a witchy tale set during the time of the Holy Roman Empire, which switched creative directors earlier this ear and is one of the games Ubi are keen to get out of the door. What Quebec have been up to since Shadows shipped is less clear. They're a much smaller than Montreal and were founded in 2005.

Ubisoft have been carrying out mass cuts across their studios worldwide all the way through this year. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx. Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona. Long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm. Ubisoft's Paris HQ. Three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz. All have been subjected to some form of cuts or closure.

Meanwhile. changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Solidarity to all of the Ubisoft workers who've been affected by these layoffs in Montreal and Quebec.

#3800. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was October's biggest game in the US, but it wasn't enough to crack 2026's best-selling top 10

Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other big-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:

Away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were new releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a big slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:

In Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything new, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested."

The console release of GTA 6 is here, in case you hadn't noticed. And us PC gamers are desperate to get hold of a version of our own, particularly as modders say it'll be playable on god's own platform within a week. Be careful what you click on, though, as NordVPN's threat intelligence team has discovered a nasty-sounding scam package on the dark web.

The company has posted a warning on X of a "GTA 6 PC scam kit" doing the rounds on the more dubious parts of the internet, using a fake GTA 6 PC port as bait.

A “GTA 6 PC scam kit” — yours for just $200. That’s what our Threat Intelligence team found on the dark web: a crypto wallet drainer, a fake “GTA6 Keygen.exe” that steals accounts, a YouTube Shorts bot to spread it, and a hidden crypto miner. The bait? A fake “GTA 6 PC Port.” But GTA 6 is console-only — there's no PC version coming on launch day. If you see one, it’s a scam. If it doesn’t come from the creators, don't click it!November 19, 2026

The package is said to be for sale for $200, or twice what a single copy of Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition costs at retail. Included is a crypto wallet drainer, a fake "GTA6 Keygen.exe," and a hidden crypto miner. There's also a YouTube Shorts bot within the package, designed to help it spread.

All of which sounds comprehensively designed to screw over PC gamers looking to get their hands on GTA 6 ahead of an official release.

Speaking to Tech Radar ahead of the games launch, NordVPN CTO Marijus Briedis said: "Someone has packaged the whole scam and is selling it to anyone with $200. You don’t need any technical skills anymore."

"People who play on PC have been waiting for news, and any link promising an early PC version will get clicks," says Briedis. "There is no PC version on November 19. If you see one, it's a scam."

NordVPN isn't the only security provider warning of GTA 6 scams. Malwarebytes has detailed a number of dodgy sites that supposedly offer access to the game, each using the hype as a lure to convince you to give away your details and funnel you into various schemes.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

All of which compels me to restate the facts: GTA 6 does not have a PC release at the time of writing. In fact, it's not even been announced by Rockstar at this point. The game is available in Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5 versions only, and while modders seem to be beavering away on an unofficial PC version based on a leaked Xbox build, it's not available yet.

Don't let yourself be fooled into clicking shady links—and if you don't have a console like my good self, be prepared to wait. May I suggest playing all the other excellent games in your Steam backlog instead? It's not like we're short of PC games in general, you know.

I don't know how you follow a $1.8 billion trip through Greek mythology, but Steven Spielberg apparently has an idea. Christopher Nolan is still taking a victory lap for The Odyssey, one of the biggest hits on the 2026 movie schedule, and the Jaws director just floated a follow-up I'd pay good money to see. The way he brought it up made me laugh, too. Even Hollywood legends know how to suggest another movie without sounding too pushy.

The moment came Tuesday, Nov. 17, at an awards-season screening of The Odyssey in Los Angeles. Spielberg moderated a Q&A with Nolan at the Directors Guild of America theater, where he praised the filmmaker's latest blockbuster before slipping in one more suggestion. As Gizmodo's Germain Lussier reported from the event, Spielberg told him:

The only other thing I want to say, not to challenge you or anything, but there’s always The Iliad.

I love how politely Spielberg slid that into the conversation. It's the cinematic equivalent of complimenting somebody's enormous Thanksgiving dinner and then asking what they're making next year. He even followed it up by insisting there was no pressure. Nolan, understandably, joked that Spielberg seemed to be speaking for Universal Pictures. Spielberg admitted the studio would probably appreciate it, but he was interested himself.

The idea makes a lot of sense. Homer's The Iliad takes place during the Trojan War, before Odysseus spends years trying to get home in The Odyssey. It wouldn't be a straightforward sequel, since we'd be going backward in the timeline, but the stories share a world. Imagine Nolan using his massive practical sets and IMAX cameras to tackle the conflict between Achilles and Hector. I'm already looking for a seat.

Here's what really makes the suggestion fun: Nolan almost got his shot at The Iliad decades ago. He was originally hired to direct Troy, the 2004 movie that eventually went to Wolfgang Petersen and starred Brad Pitt as Achilles. Nolan has since explained that he carried ideas from that unrealized project into The Odyssey, including the impressive Trojan Horse sequence.

Nolan has already explained why he chose The Odyssey. He considers The Iliad more grounded, while the later poem's monsters and stranger adventures offered something he hadn't seen done the way he envisioned. That doesn't mean he couldn't change his mind, especially after his latest movie has reportedly earned more than $1.8 billion worldwide.

There's also something delightful about Spielberg being the person to make this pitch. He helped develop Interstellar before Nolan took over, and Nolan consulted him while preparing Dunkirk. Watching Spielberg praise Nolan as a fellow filmmaker and then immediately ask for another movie feels like the most recognizable fan behavior imaginable.

For now, Nolan hasn't announced his next directing project. He told the crowd that he tends to focus on one film at a time and figures out the next one only after he's finished. So nobody should start booking tickets for The Iliad just yet. But if the man who gave us Jaws, Raiders of the Lost Ark, and Jurassic Park is personally asking for another giant Homer adaptation, I think somebody at Universal should at least write that suggestion down. Maybe keep the IMAX cameras handy.

In the meantime, The Odyssey is now available to rent or buy digitally, as well as on Blu-ray and 4K Blu-ray.

#3797. Ignore that other game about crime that's out and burgle some ugly farmhouses in Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" with a 2000s Cartoon Network vibe

Is there something going on today? A lot of talk about committing crimes and the like, I just can't quite put my finger on why… Ah well, couldn't be important or interesting. What is interesting, however, is Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" that has launched on this inauspicious day about stealing stuff from "hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere."

With the sarcastic intro out the way, I will address the elephant in the room: Vovly's Adventure: Reslimed is out today too. Fine, fine, yes I know GTA 6 is the game everyone's talking about, but Forward Instinct, the devs behind Keepsake County, seem well aware of that in their launch day post for the game: "Folks, thanks for your incredible patience. Keepsake County is finally OUT! And yes, it is deeply ironic that it wound up being today, of all days, that we got the green light to finally release, but here we are."

Keepsake Country was supposed to release earlier this month, but seemingly got caught up in the backlog Valve are faced with that's undoubtedly been caused by genAI games. In any case, the burgle-em-up does look quite delightful. I'm not sure if I can quite put my finger on exactly why I get this feeling, but it calls to mind a more complex version of the kind of game you'd find on Cartoon Network's website back in the day (which is a high point of praise, I'd like to be clear).

Each house in Keepsake Country is procedurally generated, meaning you never quite know what to expect when you enter. There's lockpicking, resident tie upping, and of course stealing to be done, but it doesn't just stop at the house. Parking your car, for instance, is an important thing to consider; do you want it hidden so you're less likely to be discovered, or right at the front door so you can make a speedy escape? Not to mention you have to deal with the fuzz showing up at some point if you aren't quick enough!

Gear and the like can be improved between runs, meaning you can lockpick faster or delay the cops, it all seems quite systemically thoughtful. Very much some immersive sim vibes from this one, just on a much smaller scale. And most certainly worth considering picking up on a release day like today! If you're interested in doing so, you can pick it up on Steam right here.

#3796. As Rockstar's alleged "union busting" tribunal hearing comes to a close amid GTA 6 launch, judge pledges to deliver verdict "as quickly as I possibly can"

Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's currently no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

The case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

People Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can."

However, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog."

One fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they said. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the new depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it."

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

Additionally, Rockstar employees are currently voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

#3793. Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

Still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

But nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity quickly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

It's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of New Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

Again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

More impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

#3792. Warren Spector lambasts GTA 6's "billion dollar" development - 'I just hope it's is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer'

"A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries."

As GTA 6 finally arrives, increasingly outspoken games industry legend Warren Spector - known for seminal immersive sims including Deus Ex - has offered both praise for the game's achievements and lambasted its "billion dollar" development model, writing, "I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it’s the best we have to offer".

Spector announced his retirement from games development in August following struggles at his OtherSide Entertainment studio, and has been vocal about the state of the games industry in the months since, notably saying anyone at EA responsible for the "travesty" of BioWare's closure should be "ashamed". And now Spector has taken on GTA 6.

"First, congratulations to everyone who worked on GTA 6. It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "However… its billion dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate.

"That's especially true," Spector continued, "when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries. Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is."

The "sure success" of GTA 6 proves a point he's made "for years", he said: "That no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget". Highlighting GTA 6's year-long delay and reported billion dollar budget, Spector suggested, "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready [is] guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has.

"So, again, congratulations," Spector concluded. "Ambition and innovation are necessary for the medium to reach its potential. I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer."

Despite Spector's concerns, GTA 6's arrival is, as expected, already causing shockwaves across the industry. It has broken pre-order records for Xbox and PlayStation stores, smashed the all-time livestream viewer record, and apparently briefly broke Reddit too. And is its success deserved? Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell thinks so, saying it "pushes back the horizon of video games once again" in his five star GTA 6 review.

Back in 2021—which feels like an age ago now—Rockstar added a weird picture to a house in San Andreas in its Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy—The Definitive Edition. It captured a small UFO hovering over a cream coloured bungalow with two palm trees in its front garden. It stood out because unlike some of the other pictures, players weren't really sure where it came from, but now we have an answer: It came from the future—bet you didn't see that one coming.

Well, actually some people did see it coming as they took it to be a tiny easter egg for a future GTA's Florida-setting, which we now know is correct. The picture wasn't just hinting at the location of Grand Theft Auto 6, though, it actually depicts a real location that players can go visit.

I saw this thanks to xGarbett's easter egg video, but quickly sent our own Mollie Taylor after the scent. After driving around Belville for a little while we found it: the UFO house. Mystery solved—or was it? Well as it turns out you can go into this house during the day and inside is yet another mystery.

Walking into the garage of this home, players will be met by a sprawling mind map plastered across the wall with "IT'S A SIMULATION" written in big red letters in the middle. Oh dear, an NPC has gained sentience.

There are other phrases across the cork board such as:

I'm no psychologist, but this may be an issue.

We didn't encounter the owner of this house, luckily, but there were brochures scattered around about a boat. Seems like he's going to try and head for the open ocean in a bid to break through the map and finally gain freedom. Good luck buddy, I wish you well. Hopefully, if it all goes sideways out there the jetski dog will help him out—that'll probably make it on the conspiracy dream board.

Word is out that Elon Musk has invested a significant amount of money in Skydance, making him part-owner of the newly merged studio alongside David Ellison. With headlines suggesting the company may sell DC Studios and make other changes, I'm most concerned and have my eye on what the plan is for Star Trek.

It's been a tough year for Star Trek fans, despite it being the 60th anniversary. The year was marked by news that there are no new shows on the horizon, and ended with the passing of Walter Koenig and, of course, the death of Patrick Stewart. As the year ends, I have mixed feelings about what the future holds and how these two men may impact it in 2027 and beyond. Let's talk about it.

Ellison had a history with Star Trek before becoming head of the studio that owns it. Skydance helped co-produce both Star Trek: Into Darkness and Beyond alongside Paramount when they were separate studios, and he was on the record as a card-carrying Trekkie.

The CEO quickly mentioned Star Trek upon taking over Paramount in its original merger, and got the ball rolling on a new film. Unfortunately, we've seen this song and dance before with Paramount, as the issue was never developing a new Trek movie, but rather getting far enough along that it actually screens in theaters.

Additionally, Star Trek has zero shows in active development at this time. With no new announcements about any progress on that front, it feels as though the game plan is to let the final seasons of Strange New Worlds and Starfleet Academy air in 2027, and then maybe announce a new direction for the franchise. That's just an optimistic guess, however, as we've gotten no confirmation that is the plan.

Which brings me to the main problem I've had with David Ellison thus far. He's stated that Star Trek has a big role in what he wants to do with the future of Skydance, but we aren't really seeing any evidence of that. Right now, it feels like a lesser priority, something on the back burner, if you will, and I'm worried about just how long that will be the case.

Elon Musk's entry into Star Trek puts another alleged Trekkie at the top of Skydance's ladder, which could propel moves into happening sooner rather than later. For those who don't know, Musk is actually a canon figure in the universe, having been directly mentioned by Gabriel Lorca as one of the great minds of humanity. Despite his various movie and film appearances, Musk has never appeared in Trek.

As A Star Trek Fan I'm Eternally Grateful For What Patrick Stewart Did For The Franchise

He's also preached about recreating Star Trek in real life via his SpaceX company, but has simultaneously butted heads with other fans in interpreting what the series is about. We saw that when Starfleet Academy came out, and he openly joked about the show having obese actors and people wearing eyeglasses.

Perhaps he was not privy to Gene Roddenberry's view that looks wouldn't matter in an idealized society. It doesn't seem to be the only message he missed, as Musk has openly criticized the franchise's embrace of diversity and inclusion, two major principles Roddenberry stressed from the beginning.

I feel as though Musk loves the part of Star Trek that is about space exploration, especially with it matching his eventual goal for humanity to expand and colonize other planets. It's imperative, however, for him to also understand the bit that the series is a morality play, and without that bit included, it ceases to be the franchise that's thrived for 60 years.

Now, it's entirely possible David Ellison and Elon Musk keep their hands out of Star Trek, and entrust someone else to do what they think will make it most successful. As it stands right now, I have my apprehensions about either being too hands-on with it, but maybe I'll be surprised a year from now.

Star Trek remains available to stream on Paramount+. I'm waiting for those final seasons of Starfleet Academy and Strange New Worlds, and hoping that movie goes into production by the end of next year.

#3789. Valve are pausing Steam Machine 2TB orders over "supply constraints," though the 512GB model is free of its waitlist

Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

It's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build new ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

Of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained."

"We anticipate having more information to share come January."

#3788. Does GTA 6 have an 'easy mode'? Not officially, but there are two very important settings you can change to make the game less difficult

By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

Toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

"We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all."

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

If you're playing GTA 6 on Xbox, you should turn off your console's automatic upload feature or you could risk having your Xbox account suspended. An Xbox user on Reddit reported receiving a two-day, unrepealable ban for automatically uploading a 28-second clip of GTA 6 characters at the beach. According to the Reddit user, sangobar, the clip was almost immediately flagged by the Xbox Network for either violating the Xbox Community Standards or Microsoft Services Agreement terms (the email they received from Xbox doesn't specify which). However, the user claims the clip only showed characters in beachwear and the clip was therefore incorrectly flagged.So, to avoid the risk of an Xbox ban it is better to be safe than sorry, to disable your Xbox automatic upload feature, and to understand what Xbox's guidelines are around the content you can upload to the Xbox Network.

Automatic uploads to the Xbox Network are enabled as standard on Xbox, meaning the GTA 6 clips you capture on your console are automatically uploaded to the Xbox Network. To turn off your Xbox Series X's automatic uploads feature, follow these steps:

One Drive is more lenient in what you can upload, but if you'd rather not automatically upload any of your GTA 6 capture, it's best to set both it and Xbox Network to 'Don't Upload'.

GTA 6 clips could potentially violate the 'Keep your content clean' term of the Xbox Community Standards, specifically the 'Make stuff that's suitable for all audiences rule', which states: "The Xbox community must be friendly and accessible to everyone, this isn't the appropriate place for sexual content. Keep your public posts and messages suitable for all ages and audiences."

According to Xbox, some examples of content that could violate this term include sharing or distributing non-consensual intimate imagery, links or imagery that displays pornography, screenshots or game clips that include mature sexual content, custom gamerpics that contains nudity, lewd messages to other players, and distasteful or inappropriate pictures. In other words, be careful before sharing images or clips of GTA 6's more mature content, like GTA 6 strip clubs.

#3785. GTA 6 leaker claims to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of Rockstar's crimsim onto the net, shouts that the "community will have it emulated inside a week"

Cyberleek, the GTA 6 leaker or leakers who shared a bunch of alleged gameplay earlier this year, are now claiming to have released a nearly complete in-development build of the crimsim's Xbox version. Continuing their established grift, the leaker or leakers are threatening to release the main executable file they've withheld unless people pump up the value of their cryptocurrency.

"It is done," a statement posted on Cyberleek’s website claimed. "CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one - the main executable - held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons."

So, more anime villain chatter from Cyberleek, who claim the executable file is on a timer and will be released immediately if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. It looks like the build is yet to be confirmed as genuine.

If any build leak were to result in GTA 6 being emulated on PC in rapid fashion, that would threaten to undercut an official port. Rockstar have yet to confirm that such a port is on the way and when it'll drop, but an October report from GamesBeat claimed the first three months of 2027 as the window in which Rockstar plan to deliver the game to PC. Former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij recently told our Edwin he reckons that concerns about unofficial ports based on the console version of GTA 6, likely made with generative AI, might lead Rockstar not to leave too big a gap before bringing the crimsim to PC officially.

Any alleged playable unofficial port of GTA 6 made with help from genAI and chucked online could, of course, just be a great big pile of malware.

Rockstar, who previously called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking", as well as parent company Take-Two, looked to have begun a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August.

We’ve always known there would come a point when the story would tell us it wants to end, and it’s our belief that our job — our responsibility — is to listen. Telling this emotional, wild, and deeply human story has been a profoundly meaningful experience and a true honor for us, and we’re so very grateful to the brilliant cast, crew and writers who have bravely gone on the journey with us to bring it to life. Most of all, we want to thank the fans who have stuck with us through every moment, mystery and meal — the Hive is nothing without you! We can’t wait to share the final chapter with you and hope you find it…delicious"

Tom is a freelance writer, predominantly focusing on film and TV. A graduate of Film Studies at University of South Wales, if he's not diving in to the Collector's Edition Blu Ray of an obscure 80s horror, you'll find him getting lost with his dog or mucking about in the water with his board.

#3782. Amid a year of layoffs, Ubisoft yank the cover off Motherbrain, their new studio "focused on AI for gameplay innovation"

Something something "proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators" something something

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "new operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said.

You'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec said. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing plan with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months."

That'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the company affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

#3781. Over 2 million Xbox players in the UK and US reportedly used the 'New Zealand trick' to play GTA 6 early - that's more than a third of the country's population

We already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'New Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

Here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 launched at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, New Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

In fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox users in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the New Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:

Amusingly, New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."

Some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Finding the Slim Jim in Chapter 2 is essential if you want to get better at stealing vehicles

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Stealing cars in GTA 6 is one of the easiest ways to attract attention from the police, thanks to the new Wanted system. You've probably noticed by now that breaking into vehicles is noisy and messy, with Jason and Lucia needing to smash the window to get inside. It also takes time – precious time in which some nosey onlooker can report your description and activity to the cops. There has to be an easier way, right? There is. Which is why you need to learn how to get a Slim Jim in GTA 6.

The Slim Jim in GTA 6 is only available from Chapter 2 onwards. This essential carjacking tool will unlock as part of the main GTA 6 mission list, coming into your possession after you begin a quest called 'Moses'. It's in this mission where you'll meet your first vehicle fence, learn how to sell cars and bikes in GTA 6, and be given the information you need to better survey vehicles for security features with the WAiNK app – which can be activated at any time by holding Up on the D-pad.

Moses will give you the Slim Jim as a part of this mission. It'll let you get into any vehicle without needing to smash the window. You will, however, still need to contend with security features – you'll have to wait until Chapter 3 to learn how to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 and understand how to deactivate trackers in GTA 6 to steal more modern vehicles.

Once you've got it, using the Slim Jim is GTA 6 is easy enough. Walk up to any vehicle you want to try and steal. Walk up to the driver-side or passenger door, and press Triangle/Y to bring out your Slim Jim. From there, it's a case of rotating the right thumbstick in a curve until you find the sweet spot – which you'll spot by rumble in the controller and by a slightly pink hue to the semi-circle indicator. Eventually you'll hear a little pop, meaning you can now climb inside.

#3779. Akira Kurabayashi, company director at Arika and developer on Street Fighter EX, Tetris 99, Fighting EX Layer and more, has sadly passed away due to heart failure

As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:

"We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you showed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul."

#3778. Ubisoft cuts jobs at major Assassin's Creed and Far Cry studios as its year of layoffs continues

Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It says the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, said to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture announced last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources."

These latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" announced by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

I can't be the only one who's ever wondered what it would be like to spend a night in the mall.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Spoiler alert! This story discusses the ultimate winners of the reality competition series Win the Mall, now available with a Netflix subscription.

Somehow Netflix has become the place to go if you want to watch a reality TV competition set in an unexpected location. (Hey, Wonka’s The Golden Ticket, I’m looking at you.) I enjoyed and see more potential in Win the Mall in the future, the one thing that became immediately clear is that I would like to see more of the actual mall itself.

It’s a simple idea. I mean, who hasn’t thought about at least spending the night in a mall, going on a shopping spree, and having free rein of the food court before sleeping in one of the mattress store’s beds? Clearly, it’s not just me, or there wouldn’t be this 2026 TV schedule release. I just wish we could have seen even more of the mall!

When you move 10 teams of two contestants into a shopping mall to compete for a $1 million grand prize, it feels like you should have a plan to incorporate the mall as much as possible. Part shopping spree and part social strategy, players are dropped into a real mall, but the fake storefronts make it challenging to fully utilize the mall itself, leaving it all to feel a bit disconnected at times.

The shopping spree challenges are the most fun because they see the teams ripping through the stores to guess what things cost to get close to their given dollar amount. It best embraces the chaos and energy of a shopping mall, especially on Black Friday. Something felt perfectly fitting about book-ending the season with shopping sprees, to introduce us to the competitors in the beginning and to narrow it down to the ultimate winner at the end. But that left six episodes in between where I wish I could have seen more of the actual mall.

There are a lot of challenges that take place adjacent to the stores, but I wish they’d found a better way to incorporate them. There’s a Starbucks in play, but we never really see the inside of it. And there’s a KFC boasted about for its lounge, but they only briefly hang out there. I just feel like there could have been some inventive ways to incorporate some of the stores themselves instead of having so many challenges set in the center space.

Surprisingly, one of the highlights of Win the Mall is TikTok creator-turned-host Haley Baylee, who is truly delightful. She’s a likable host who can wear anything and look like she’s on a runway, but she also never takes herself too seriously, being goofy when she needs to be and taking on a more serious persona while tempting contestants with possible game advantages.

Whether there’s ever another season of Win the Mall or not, I hope that we get to see more of her in the future. If we do get more, I just hope they can find a way to be more inventive in showing off more of the mall or even some “mall employees.” I liked a lot of the rest of the setup, and the contestants who ultimately won, but one possible idea is to incorporate some sort of sidekick for Haley Baylee who could be more directly related to the mall itself and could work as a bridge between the setting and the contestants. Just spitballing here.

There are a lot of great Netflix reality TV shows these days to choose from, including Squid Game: The Challenge, based on their own scripted programming. And while it wasn’t perfect, Win the Mall was entertaining and creative enough that I’d definitely watch another season. Don't let this one be a one and done, Netflix.

GameStop boss Ryan Cohen (last seen attempting to buy eBay) has called for the return of physical game discs, lamenting the lack of control players have over digital purchases in a chat with Bloomberg held on the eve of Grand Theft Auto 6's release.

In case you missed it, a media meteor impacted yesterday and blasted our landscape free of life. Grand Theft Auto 6 is here and—despite our Ted Litchfield's noble attempts to get you all thinking about Queen's Domain instead (you should play Queen's Domain)—it's all the world can talk about. It's also only available digitally.

"Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop", said Cohen, remarking that players ought to be able to do with their purchased games as they will: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend". Cohen did not namecheck GTA 6 specifically, but did say that he had been speaking about this issue with all "the obvious" publishers.

GameStop, of course, makes a tidy chunk of change from resales of games traded in at its stores—a segment of its business that becomes impossible to maintain in a world without physical discs for players to bring in and sell. Publishers oppose trade-ins "because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new", says Cohen, accusing them of "taking away competition" by restricting sales to digital-only channels.

GTA 6 is a portent of the world to come. Earlier this year, Sony announced that PlayStation would drop physical discs starting in January 2028, and has held firm to that course in the face of a vocal player uproar.

Issues around game ownership have reached the point that politicians are weighing in: last month US lawmaker Richie Torres announced the Power To The Players Act, that would prompt the US Federal Trade Commission to protect players' access to purchased games, even in the case of online-only games that get unplugged.

"When you pay for a game, you should own it", said Torres. "Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale".

#3775. Vote now for 2026's RPS 100: Reader Edition

For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

However, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we currently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

This does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

We also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have said about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

#3774. GTA 6 players are being abducted by aliens and knocked out by Bigfoot

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

And that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game launched in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

Either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 launched today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."

One half of GTA 6's leading couple, Jason Duval, is unusually reserved and soft-spoken when compared to many of the crime series' boisterous, sometimes gleefully violent protagonists. Why the change? Rockstar Games' narrative lead says the idea came from 1972's The Getaway and Jason's military background.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway," senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, says in a statement given to Destructoid.

The crime flick's star Steve McQueen "was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries continues, and that's an energy the team at Rockstar wanted to somewhat match with Jason's characterisation. Although, he also acknowledges that "so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Think Trevor and the like.

"This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders). These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries adds.

The game itself definitely plays on those ideas, too. (Something noted in our GTA 6 review.) Jason isn't the most forthcoming or chatty protagonist, but what he leaves unsaid and when he chooses to communicate is just as important as what he actually shares with Lucia - the other, more chaotic half of the game's central couple, who balances things out somewhat.

"Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe also said of the game's sweeping story. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either. The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world."

#3772. Nvidia's latest graphics card driver appears to be unnecessarily writing to PC SSDs, something that's dumb, annoying and definitely warrants reverting

Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.

As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.

Some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour. For context, it'd take a bugged driver writing that much thousands of hours to break a gaming SSD with a typical endurance rating in the hundreds of terabytes. However, that doesn't mean this is anything less than a pretty bad bug. As such, reverting to the previous driver, 621.01, is a good idea if you're on 621.24 and suspect it of writing chunks of gigabytes to your SSD.

In order to check if that's going on, open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do a bit of maths to work out if it's writing mere MB or globs of GB.

Bizarrely, the affected 621.24 driver still hasn't been pulled by Nvidia as of writing, meaning it can still be downloaded by people who might not be aware of any issues and think 'ooh, haven't checked I'm on the latest driver in a while.' The driver was released on November 12th, so it's not a brand new arrival that the company just haven't had a chance to look into yet.

Here's hoping that it is fixed or replaced ASAP, if it hasn't been by the time you read this. AMD look to have dealt with a similar issue recently, and I'd like to think driver updates across all cards aren't going to be some form of permanent Russian roulette going forwards.

#3771. World of Warcraft: Forever has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years, says Blizzard

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

"Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!"

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the new edition.

Since it launched on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard said WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players.

For the last decade, Ben and Erin Napier have been renovating homes in the small Southern town of Laurel, Mississippi, on HGTV’s wildly popular show Home Town. The series’ 10th season premiered in January on the 2026 TV schedule, and fans, including me, have been itching for any sort of update on the famous reality couple. In particular, I’ve been waiting for an update on Season 11, and Erin finally spoke out.

Season 10 wrapped up in March, and Erin revealed in August that filming had just started back up on the new episodes. While there isn’t any information on when to expect Home Town''s exact return, there is one big piece of news that will surely make people happy: Erin took to her social channels earlier this week to share the episodes are just about done, and she even posted photos from the wrap party:

A post shared by Erin Napier (@erinapier)

Considering it’s been a trying year for the Napiers, it’s great to see them finally able to celebrate something. Last December, the hotel they were renovating for their series, Home Town: Inn This Together, caught on fire, close to Erin’s 40th birthday.

Fans were able to see the hard work the couple and their team have put into the hotel for the spinoff, which ended with the hotel fire (streaming now with an HBO Max subscription), but I love that they can look forward to the future of Home Town, which is certainly not slowing down any time soon thanks to the Napiers and their incredible team:

Season 10 will be all buttoned up in a couple of weeks but last night we celebrated. You all must know that there’s no way one person can manage the design processes of 9 houses at the same time, and so I get to lean on this incredible team. Together we make a plan then everyone goes on whatever journey the house gives them, shopping and making every design choice with me. They are the many eyes and hands and feet that get to these houses across the finish line and I get to be an editor in chief of sorts, and it feels like magic every time.

Welp, I didn't see this confusion coming. I’m excited to see what kind of houses the Napiers are renovating in the new season, which is billed as Season 10, but is actually Season 11. The Season 10 finale aired in March, so these new batch of episodes, coming sometime in 2027, will certainly be Season 11.

It's a little confusing, and the Home Town stars know it. Erin clarified why she referred to the new episodes as Season 10, rather than Season 11, when asked by a fan, and her response makes a lot of sense:

So, because of a programming discrepancy like 4 years ago, the numbers are off! y'all will know Season 10 as Season 11.

It’s definitely confusing, but I'm glad it was addressed. There are plenty of shows whose production numbers don’t line up with episode numbers, for whatever reason. For instance, a big Jeopardy! inconsistency Ken Jennings revealed last year was that the production numbers currently being used don’t equal the total number of episodes produced, all because of mistakes from decades ago.

Regardless, I’m relieved to know production is just about wrapped, meaning we’ll be getting the Napiers back on our TVs soon. It's also worth noting, new seasons of Home Town typically premiere in December or January, and since the new season is still being worked on for the next couple of weeks, if the pattern sticks, we could be looking the same timeline for Season 10 (11). For now, the wait continues!
